# apicp_web_domain (Resource)

Manages a web vhost (nginx-served domain) in apicp.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apicp_web_domain" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

# One vhost can answer to several names. Each alias serves the same files as the domain and is
# covered by the same certificate; every name must resolve to the node.
resource "apicp_web_domain" "with_www" {
  domain  = "example.org"
  aliases = ["www.example.org"]
}

resource "apicp_tls_certificate" "with_www" {
  vhost_id = apicp_web_domain.with_www.id
}

# A Node.js app instead of static files or PHP: deploy it into /home/<unix_user>/app over SSH
# (see apicp_ssh_access), build it, then touch ~/app/restart.txt. EmDash and other Astro sites
# work with the default start file, dist/server/entry.mjs.
resource "apicp_web_domain" "node_app" {
  domain       = "app.example.net"
  node_version = "24"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain name, e.g. `example.com`. Changing this renames the vhost in place (apicp removes the old nginx config and reapplies under the new domain) rather than replacing the resource.

### Optional

- `aliases` (Set of String) Extra host names this vhost serves from the same document root, e.g. `www.example.com`. Lower case; each name must be unique across all vhosts (as a domain or an alias) and must resolve to the node. One `apicp_tls_certificate` covers the domain and every alias: adding an alias to a domain that already has a certificate orders a new one for all the names (if that fails the apply fails and nothing changes); removing an alias orders nothing, and the next automatic renewal leaves the name out.
- `app_entry` (String) The Node.js app's start file, relative to `~/app`. Omit for `dist/server/entry.mjs`, what Astro's Node adapter (and EmDash) builds.
- `node_version` (String) Run a Node.js app for this domain instead of static files or PHP: `22` or `24`. apicp runs it as the domain's Unix user from `/home/<unix_user>/app` (deploy it there over SSH, then touch `~/app/restart.txt`), listening on `127.0.0.1:app_port`, and nginx proxies to it. Cannot be set together with `php_version`. Setting it back to `""` (or removing it) stops and removes the app's service; its files stay.
- `php_version` (String) PHP-FPM version to serve this domain with: `5.6`, `7.2`, `7.4`, `8.0`, `8.1`, `8.2`, `8.3`, or `8.4`. Omit (or set to `""`) for static content only, the default — apicp never installs a PHP version itself, a domain can only select one already provisioned on its node. Cannot be set together with `node_version`.

### Read-Only

- `app_port` (Number) The loopback port apicp gave the Node.js app (passed to it as `PORT`); 0 without `node_version`.
- `document_root` (String) Filesystem path apicp serves this domain from.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `node_id` (String) The apicp node this vhost is provisioned on. apicp's current single-node MVP always assigns its one configured node — this attribute is read-only, not settable, since the API does not yet honor a caller-supplied node selection.
- `status` (String)
- `tls_enabled` (Boolean) Whether a TLS certificate is currently installed — managed via `apicp_tls_certificate`, not directly on this resource.
- `unix_user` (String) Per-domain Unix user apicp created for filesystem isolation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apicp_web_domain.example vh_abc123
```
